blogs.title: Math in Web Pages: How DeepSeek Math Found Genius in Sea of Data
blogs.description: Discover how the DeepSeekMath team cracked the code to train a top-tier math model using only publicly available web data from Common Crawl. We break down their unique 'iterative mining' pipeline that filters billions of tokens to create a high-quality, multilingual (especially Chinese) math corpus, proving you don't need arXiv papers to teach an AI math.

blogs.title: GRPO: The Memory-Saver Backend Revolutionizing RL for LLMs
blogs.description: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is crucial for sharpening AI reasoning, but it's rarely used because it requires massive computing power and memory. Dive into Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), the new algorithm introduced by DeepSeek that eliminates the heavy 'critic model' component of PPO, allowing for faster, cheaper, and more efficient training on math problems.

blogs.title: Why Code Training Makes a Better Mathematician Than You Thought
blogs.description: There's a common belief that reading research papers (like those on arXiv) is best for teaching math to AIs. The DeepSeekMath paper challenges this, showing that starting with 'code training' before math leads to superior reasoning capabilities and helps prevent the AI from 'forgetting' how to code. We explore their experiments comparing code-heavy vs. paper-heavy pre-training strategies.

blogs.title: Closing the Gap: How a Tiny 7B Model is Beating Massive Competitors
blogs.description: GPT-4 wins on complex math tasks because it has Trillions of parameters and secret training data. But DeepSeekMath proves you can get close to that performance with just 7 Billion parameters! We analyze the 'Secret Sauce' behind this open-source leader: high-quality data curation and strategic Reinforcement Learning, and what this means for the future of open-source AI.
